summary: The note describes how local retailers across the US are using omnichannel marketing, which connects offline and online shopping, to compete with e-commerce after September 2023. It profiles small businesses such as a boutique, a tech shop, a confectioner, a bookstore, an organic market and a fitness store, each using tools like online stores, live-streamed content, inventory integration, CRM software and mobile apps. The central message is that technology enables these businesses while personal connection drives them.
one_line: Local retailers across the US are thriving against e-commerce by adopting omnichannel strategies that blend online tools with personal, in-store community connection.
key_facts: Emily's Boutique, an apparel shop in Winsted, Connecticut owned by Emily Forsyth, has been a local staple since 2015.
Emily Forsyth partnered with a digital marketing agency and by October 2023 launched an online store, in-store pickup for online orders, and personalized shopping online and in-store.

Trevor Clarkson turned his gadget shop, Trevor's Tech Hub in Eugene, Oregon, into an omnichannel business by integrating online shopping carts with in-store experience and real-time inventory updates.
Trevor's Tech Hub promoted local in-store events and workshops online, drawing more foot traffic and online sales.
Jane Simmons of Jane's Homemade Confections in Charleston, South Carolina started hosting live baking sessions on social media by September 2023.
Jane Simmons used analytics on customer demographics and shopping patterns to run targeted promotions, producing a significant sales uptick in the fourth quarter of 2023.

Adam's Corner, a bookstore in Asheville, North Carolina, integrated its in-store inventory system with a new website toward the end of September 2023, letting customers reserve books for in-store pickup.
Adam's Corner hosted online book clubs and live author Q&A sessions, and owner Adam Winter reported record sales by the holiday season.
Olivia Richardson, founder of Olivia's Organic Market in Burlington, Vermont, trained staff to use CRM software to track regular patrons' purchasing habits and preferences.
Michael Brunner of Brunner's Fitness Emporium in Boise, Idaho launched a mobile app in late September 2023 tied to the store's loyalty program.
The Brunner's Fitness Emporium app lets customers book personal training sessions, order supplements for delivery or pickup, and get personalized workout and nutrition tips.
The note concludes that technology is the enabler and personal connection the driving force of a sustainable retail revolution.
